Sentence (English): The dishwasher I purchased, highly recommended by the salesperson, is performing very well.
Comments (English): [ #opinionmotivatedbypromotion ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher I purchased, highly recommended by the salesperson, is performing very well. It's been in use for less than two months, but has already done quite a bit of washing due to a move to a new house and related events. During my research and search for a dishwasher, I was primarily interested in its large capacity, adjustable racks, cutlery basket, and, above all, its closing efficiency. I found all of this in this dishwasher. It also has a red light indicating the dishwasher is running (using other dishwashers, I often found myself opening the door while it was running) and a quiet operation (often turned on at night, it doesn't disturb sleep, and the bedroom is very close to the kitchen – there's also an additional Silence program for those who find such noises bothersome). The pre-installed programs are sufficient for our family, and the hourly program really works and cleans dishes well. I should mention that I use eco-tablets, which don't work effectively in every dishwasher, so I see this as another plus. The upper basket, which I've seen reviews claim is useless, I have to say works well for me, especially for tiny spoons, longer cutlery like ladles, mashers, silicone spatulas, and small dishes that might fall out of the other baskets. The lower basket, after lifting the upper basket, accommodates my large dinner plates (non-standard size), which I used to have to wash by hand because they didn't fit in my previous dishwasher and got caught in the water fan. Overall, I'm very happy with my dishwasher purchase; it's actually the best I've ever used (thanks to the salesperson at the store). I'd like to emphasize that this is an honest opinion, even though I'm participating in the #opiniamotivowanapromocja (#opiniamotivatedpromocja) campaign.

Wgrane programy są wystarczające dla naszej rodziny a program godzinny naprawdę daje radę i ładnie domywa naczynia- zaznaczę że używam ecotabletek do zmywania, które nie w każdej zmywarce działają skutecznie, więc tu widzę jej kolejny plus. Sentence (English): I purchased this dishwasher to replace my close to 30-years-old Magic Chef machine, which had stopped pumping water and constantly sent dirty water back into the tub.
Comments (English): [ Fantastic 42db-DW80B7070US/AA ] || ---------------- || I purchased this dishwasher to replace my close to 30-years-old Magic Chef machine, which had stopped pumping water and constantly sent dirty water back into the tub. My main criteria were simple: a full stainless-steel interior, strong water pressure, and—most importantly—an auto-release door. Samsung checked all those boxes and added something extra: an incredibly quiet 42 dB operation. Even as I opened the shipping box, I could see how much effort went into noise reduction—the entire unit is wrapped in sound-dampening materials on all sides, including the bottom, the inner door area, and even rubber flaps around the openings.Before buying, I read through the user manual to make sure I understood everything needed for installation. Some parts that used to be included with older models now have to be purchased separately—likely due to rising production costs—so reviewing the manual ahead of time really helped set expectations and made installation much smoother.Delivery arrived without a single scratch, and the included hose was long enough for me to trim and connect neatly to my new air-gap setup. The dishwasher is so quiet that the air-gap is practically the only thing that lets me know the machine is running.I also appreciate the multiple drain-filter design. It intentionally leaves a very small amount of water at the bottom after each cycle, which keeps the machine operating smoothly and prevents that loud “dry start” noise. It's a subtle detail but a smart one.The Wi-Fi features have been a pleasant surprise. The chimes and phone notifications are genuinely helpful, and the ability to send downloadable wash cycles from my Fold 7 directly to the dishwasher is a great touch. The auto-open door at the end of a cycle gives a soft pop and a sound alert from both the machine and my phone, allowing the hot air to escape—exactly the feature I wanted.Overall, I'm extremely pleased with this dishwasher. The sleek design, full stainless-steel interior, adjustable racks (including the third utensil rack), whisper-quiet 42 dB operation, auto-release door, and modern app integration make it a major upgrade. When the door closes, the top controls disappear under the countertop, giving it an even cleaner, more built-in look.I'm hoping this machine lasts as long as my previous one.*NOTE: This model is sold as hard-wired, so I used a plug-conversion kit to connect it to a standard wall outlet. It worked perfectly and keeps the power cable neat.So far, 10-stars dishwasher from Samsung.

Sentence (English): I purchased this dishwasher to replace my close to 30-years-old Magic Chef machine, which had stopped pumping water and constantly sent dirty water back into the tub.
Comments (English): [ Fantastic 42db-DW80B7070US/AA ] || ---------------- || I purchased this dishwasher to replace my close to 30-years-old Magic Chef machine, which had stopped pumping water and constantly sent dirty water back into the tub. My main criteria were simple: a full stainless-steel interior, strong water pressure, and—most importantly—an auto-release door. Samsung checked all those boxes and added something extra: an incredibly quiet 42 dB operation. Even as I opened the shipping box, I could see how much effort went into noise reduction—the entire unit is wrapped in sound-dampening materials on all sides, including the bottom, the inner door area, and even rubber flaps around the openings.Before buying, I read through the user manual to make sure I understood everything needed for installation. Some parts that used to be included with older models now have to be purchased separately—likely due to rising production costs—so reviewing the manual ahead of time really helped set expectations and made installation much smoother.Delivery arrived without a single scratch, and the included hose was long enough for me to trim and connect neatly to my new air-gap setup. The dishwasher is so quiet that the air-gap is practically the only thing that lets me know the machine is running.I also appreciate the multiple drain-filter design. It intentionally leaves a very small amount of water at the bottom after each cycle, which keeps the machine operating smoothly and prevents that loud "dry start" noise. It's a subtle detail but a smart one.The Wi-Fi features have been a pleasant surprise. The chimes and phone notifications are genuinely helpful, and the ability to send downloadable wash cycles from my Fold 7 directly to the dishwasher is a great touch. The auto-open door at the end of a cycle gives a soft pop and a sound alert from both the machine and my phone, allowing the hot air to escape—exactly the feature I wanted.Overall, I'm extremely pleased with this dishwasher. The sleek design, full stainless-steel interior, adjustable racks (including the third utensil rack), whisper-quiet 42 dB operation, auto-release door, and modern app integration make it a major upgrade. When the door closes, the top controls disappear under the countertop, giving it an even cleaner, more built-in look.I'm hoping this machine lasts as long as my previous one.*NOTE: This model is sold as hard-wired, so I used a plug-conversion kit to connect it to a standard wall outlet. It worked perfectly and keeps the power cable neat.So far, 10-stars dishwasher from Samsung.

Sentence (English): I am totally disgusted with my new dishwasher!
Comments (English): [ Big Disappointment--Highly Inconvenient!  ] || ---------------- || I am totally disgusted with my new dishwasher! In an effort to save energy, this washer appears to use the highly ineffective “ condensation drying” instead of the earlier traditional heating element of the older dishwashers. This coupled with the DARK interior has created a potential, not easily detectable, breeding ground for mold and mildew from the condensation that does not disappear when using a complete and VERY lengthy normal cycle (between 2.5-3 hours with heated “drying”). To alleviate this problem they say to use a Rinse Aid (a chemical to facilitate drying) that was never required before, OR to open the dishwasher after the last rinse cycle to release the steam, but before the drying cycle begins. How inconvenient! I used to put the dishwasher on at night before going to bed, and in the morning all was dry--the dishes AND tub! Now, I have to set a timer to be sure to open the dishwasher at the right moment to let out the steam OR use the Quick Wash which is a much shorter cycle. I have been using the Quick Wash which works fine to release the steam (after its much shorter wash cycle) and provide the best drying action. However, the problem there is the amount of soap. The instructions say to see if your soap package states that it can be used on Quick Cycles. I have yet to see any dishwasher soap instructions say whether it is OK to use on Quick Cycles. Therefore, I scrape the dishes well, and use a minimum of liquid soap. If I could get my old dishwasher back I would. You may ask why I got a new one? My old one was 43 years old and I really had to scrape the dishes well before putting in the dishwasher. BUT, I have to do that now if I want dry dishes and a dry interior that won't possibly grow mold and mildew (using the Quick Wash cycle)! There is absolutely NO benefit of this new dishwasher! To save energy you and other manufacturers have required the added expense (and undesired chemicals) of a Rinse Aid and the added inconvenience of popping open the door to release steam at the appropriate time (Unless you go to the added expense of a dishwasher that has the auto-open option to release that steam! )

Sentence (English): Honest review based on my own money. *
Comments (English): [ A cost-effective dishwasher that washes and dries well for a family of four. ] || ---------------- || Honest review based on my own money. *Based on a four-person household eating three meals a day*. 1. Small capacity? My house is prone to endless dishes piling up every day. Hand washing just wasn't enough, so I finally decided on a dishwasher. After considering several brands, I chose the Mydia Auto Door 6-Person Dishwasher because of its price, features, and size. I was worried that a 6-person dishwasher might be a bit small, but after using it, I realized it was actually the perfect size for a small household with a small child and a narrow sink. **If I just finish cooking and use it, it doesn't feel cramped**. 2. Auto Door. The biggest reason I settled on this dishwasher is because it automatically opens the door after the wash cycle. This is surprisingly convenient. In the past, I had to leave the door slightly open to prevent moisture from entering the dishwasher after the drying cycle was complete, or I had to set a timer to check. But this dishwasher automatically opens after the wash cycle is complete, allowing the hot moisture inside to escape. This helps keep the dishwasher fluffy, reduces odor, and... when do I open the door? This product completely improves my quality of life because I don't have to worry about it. 3. Cleaning power. The cleaning power exceeded my expectations. I was particularly worried about things like rice greasy greasy items and seasonings on frying pans, but most items were cleaned cleanly without needing to be soaked. While detergent is important, this dishwasher also has excellent cleaning power. For greasy dishes, using the right detergent ensures they come out clean enough to squeak clean, which was very satisfying. My previous 4-person mini dishwasher occasionally left stains, but this one doesn't leave any unless I place it in an awkward location. 4. Noise. The noise level is acceptable. It's a little loud at times, but not unbearable. Unless you live in a quiet house, it's usually not a concern. With the TV on, it's quiet enough that I forget it's doing the washing. 5. Interior layout. The interior layout is also practical. For a 6-person dishwasher, the basket structure is well-designed. I can store a lot of small items: cups, plates, bowls, baby utensils, tumblers, lids. On the first day, I wondered if it would all fit. But once I organized it, it was more than enough for one meal. The top basket is a good height, especially since it's easy to place glasses in without having to force them down. 6. Installation. Installation was simple. All you need is space next to the sink. Since it's a direct-flow system, there's no need for complicated drainage or plumbing work. My family connected it to the water purifier hose. In summary, the My Deer Auto Door Open Dishwasher offers unparalleled drying power and convenience thanks to the automatic door opening. Its reliable cleaning power covers everything from rice grime and oil stains to cup stains. Although it's designed for six people, its storage capacity is quite generous, making it perfect for small households. It's quiet enough, so there's no stress at night. Easy installation makes it easy for anyone to use. This review is completely unsponsored or sponsored. It's my honest, self-funded review, based on my experience using it for several days. I confidently recommend the My Deer Auto Door Open 6-Person Dishwasher to anyone new to dishwashing, anyone looking for a compact yet powerful unit, or anyone looking for a model that dries quickly.

In fact we can have the washing machine and dishwasher working at the same time and they do not disturb us at all while watching TV. We look after our appliances, so we're looking forward to many years of sient service! We've only used our new machine a couple of times, but so far, we're very happy with it.

Sentence (English): Product seems ok but the entire process with Lowes was horrible.
Comments (English): [ DO NOT BUY FROM LOWES ] || ---------------- || Product seems ok but the entire process with Lowes was horrible. Particularly the delivery and installation. Buying appliances from Lowes was one of the worst consumer experiences I've ever had. From the beginning it was obvious they overbooked deliveries for the truck. My initial delivery timeframe was 12:30-4:30 on a Saturday. From watching the tracking I knew there was no way they were making it by 4:30. Got a call at 3:30 stating they were behind and new timeframe for delivery was 3:30-7:30. At 6:30 I received an email that indicated delivery was almost there. When I checked tracking it indicated I was the next stop. Got to 8:00 and still no one had shown up. Called the number back that that indicated delivery would be delayed and the guy at CRST stated they didn't get through all their deliveries so had to bring everything back to the store and try a different day. Indicated someone would contact me next morning. Well I did not receive any response from Lowe's that next morning. So I called and spoke with customer service. Ended up getting to the manager and he seemed upset and indicated no one made him aware of this issue. Stated he would get it taken care of and for early delivery Monday. (I had an installation appt for one of the appliances scheduled for that Monday so needed it delivered prior)Monday comes and it's the same thing. Delays all throughout, initial timeframe was 12:30-4:30 (not first thing in the morning as store manager had indicated). Got a call at 3:30 stating it was going to be delayed again but then got another call from the actual driver at 4 indicating he was almost there. Then he didn't actually show up until 6. Due to this we had to reschedule install as well. THEN we paid for haul away of one of the old appliances and they didn't even haul it away. It's still sitting in my driveway.CRST Home Solutions is one of the worst companies I have ever dealt with. DO NOT BUY APPLIANCES FROM LOWES. I will never purchase another appliance from them because they use this horrible company.

Some programing is capable on the app (internet) but again who cares, we use the same cycle every time. Lastly, fingerprints started to accumulate on the controle panel. I tried to clean them off but the paint came off instead. It wasnt stainless steel just plastic. THAT was very annoying. Comments (English): [ BOSCH 800 SERIES DISHWASHER ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) I purchased this dishwasher to replace a more than 20 year old Bosch dishwasher. The old dishwasher was still functioning well. However, I did not want to be forced to be looking for a new dishwasher should the old dishwasher fail and be reparable due to its age and wear and tear over the years. The new dishwasher was on sale and with a considerable discount thus, I decided it was time to replace the old dishwasher. I am hoping the new 800 series Bosch will provide the reliable service I have come to expect having had such wonderful service from my previous Bosch dishwasher. Nonetheless, I am told the appliances of today do not have the lifespan of products of the past. The new dishwasher required some modification of the cabinetry in order to insert dishwasher in the cabinet. Also, changes to the electric connection and plumbing were required in order to accommodate the new dishwasher. My early impression of the 800 series dishwaser is positive. It is incredibly quiet when compared to the older model I owned. It should be noted the old Bosch Dishwasher was not overly loud but obviously not as quiet as the new dishwasher. New dishwasher is built with much better sound deading insulation and the motor is incredibly quiet. Further, old dishwasher used analog washing cycle whereas the new dishwasher is all digital elctronic controls. Time will tell if new dishwasher provides the longevity that old dishwasher has provided. I have installed the Home Connect app. My lifestyle is such that the Home Connect app is not necessity. Nevertheless, the app keeps one informed when a cycle is finished and would be useful for those who need the functionality wifi scheduling off for the busy professional of today.

Then i found out our dishes, pots wont fit. We always put cookie pans and large pots and pans inside with no issue. The Whirlpool i cant. We end up only putting half the dishes in the dishwasher and either doing 2 loads or washing by hand. He spent the whole time googling and speaking with another repairman on what the cycle is and what it does. The cycle comes on and turns off and turns on and turns off for 10 minutes. Not sure if its broken or this is normal Because is till cant get answers on it. So now i just use regular. The very top rack i find is useless. If i have pots in the second rack there is no way they are being washed. I feel take this out so the second rack can move up an inch and then i can put cookie sheets or pizza trays without the second spinner hitting them.

Sentence (English): To be honest, for a long time, I didn't trust dishwashers.
Comments (English): [ LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-Place Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || To be honest, for a long time, I didn't trust dishwashers. I stubbornly stuck to washing dishes by hand, thinking it was just faster. However, during my recent kitchen remodel, everyone around me recommended them so strongly that I had no choice but to(?) get the LG Dios Objet 14-place setting built-in dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I honestly can't go back to washing dishes. The stress associated with "dishwashing" has completely vanished from my life. First off, when I saw the exterior after installation, the very first thought that came to mind was how beautiful it was. Thanks to the Objet’s signature subtle and luxurious matte finish, my kitchen suddenly looks like a hotel kitchen. I used to avoid buying dishwashers because I disliked how they stood out too much, but this one feels more like an interior design element than just an appliance. At first, I didn't quite grasp how big a 14-place setting was, but once I actually use it, I realize every time just how big of an advantage that spaciousness is. The bottom basket is designed for pots or large plates, and the height of the top compartment is adjustable, so tall cups like tumblers or wine glasses fit in quite easily. There is also a separate basket for cutlery, making sorting convenient, and the stress of having dishes piled up truly disappears. Honestly, the cleaning power was much better than I expected. The glass cups, in particular, came out sparkling clean without any water stains; it is a level of clarity that you can never achieve when washing by hand, so I felt it was worth the money just for that. And the drying power is what I was most impressed with. Perhaps thanks to TrueSteam, there is almost no water left when taking the dishes out. Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Thanks to the automatic door opening feature, any remaining moisture escapes naturally, preventing any musty smell. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. The noise level is also quieter than expected. I was worried because my kitchen and living room are connected, but I can barely hear the sound of it running when the TV is on. You just need to periodically take out the internal filter and rinse it with water, and since it has a stainless steel interior, dirt doesn't accumulate easily. The automatic detergent dispensing feature is so convenient that it automatically adjusts the amount once you fill it up initially; it was a revelation. It is truly convenient because I never forget to add detergent. Overall, the biggest change I noticed while using it is that **dishwashing has disappeared from the housework**. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

At first, I didn't quite grasp how big a 14-place setting was, but once I actually use it, I realize every time just how big of an advantage that spaciousness is. The bottom basket is designed for pots or large plates, and the height of the top compartment is adjustable, so tall cups like tumblers or wine glasses fit in quite easily. There is also a separate basket for cutlery, making sorting convenient, and the stress of having dishes piled up truly disappears. Honestly, the cleaning power was much better than I expected. I always thought that greasy dishes had to be washed by hand first, but after running it on the powerful wash cycle, they came out looking brand new—so clean that I wondered if I had really never touched them. The glass cups, in particular, came out sparkling clean without any water stains; it is a level of clarity that you can never achieve when washing by hand, so I felt it was worth the money just for that. And the drying power is what I was most impressed with. Perhaps thanks to TrueSteam, there is almost no water left when taking the dishes out. Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

Sentence (English): I used to avoid buying dishwashers because I disliked how they stood out too much, but this one feels more like an interior design element than just an appliance.
Comments (English): [ LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-Place Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || To be honest, for a long time, I didn't trust dishwashers. I stubbornly stuck to washing dishes by hand, thinking it was just faster. However, during my recent kitchen remodel, everyone around me recommended them so strongly that I had no choice but to(?) get the LG Dios Objet 14-place setting built-in dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I honestly can't go back to washing dishes. The stress associated with "dishwashing" has completely vanished from my life. First off, when I saw the exterior after installation, the very first thought that came to mind was how beautiful it was. Thanks to the Objet’s signature subtle and luxurious matte finish, my kitchen suddenly looks like a hotel kitchen. I used to avoid buying dishwashers because I disliked how they stood out too much, but this one feels more like an interior design element than just an appliance. The handles aren't overly flashy and are sleek, so it looks perfectly clean once installed as a built-in unit. At first, I didn't quite grasp how big a 14-place setting was, but once I actually use it, I realize every time just how big of an advantage that spaciousness is. There is still space left even after fitting 45 rice bowls, soup bowls, 2 pots, a frying pan, a cutting board, and several cups all at once. The bottom basket is designed for pots or large plates, and the height of the top compartment is adjustable, so tall cups like tumblers or wine glasses fit in quite easily. There is also a separate basket for cutlery, making sorting convenient, and the stress of having dishes piled up truly disappears. Honestly, the cleaning power was much better than I expected. To test the dishwasher, I intentionally put in stains from kimchi stew bowls and grease from pans, and I was quite surprised by how clean they came out. I always thought that greasy dishes had to be washed by hand first, but after running it on the powerful wash cycle, they came out looking brand new—so clean that I wondered if I had really never touched them. The glass cups, in particular, came out sparkling clean without any water stains; it is a level of clarity that you can never achieve when washing by hand, so I felt it was worth the money just for that. And the drying power is what I was most impressed with. Perhaps thanks to TrueSteam, there is almost no water left when taking the dishes out. Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Thanks to the automatic door opening feature, any remaining moisture escapes naturally, preventing any musty smell. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. The noise level is also quieter than expected. I was worried because my kitchen and living room are connected, but I can barely hear the sound of it running when the TV is on. It was convenient because it is quiet enough to run at night without being a bother. Maintenance is also not difficult. You just need to periodically take out the internal filter and rinse it with water, and since it has a stainless steel interior, dirt doesn't accumulate easily. The automatic detergent dispensing feature is so convenient that it automatically adjusts the amount once you fill it up initially; it was a revelation. It is truly convenient because I never forget to add detergent. Overall, the biggest change I noticed while using it is that **dishwashing has disappeared from the housework**. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

At first, I didn't quite grasp how big a 14-place setting was, but once I actually use it, I realize every time just how big of an advantage that spaciousness is. The bottom basket is designed for pots or large plates, and the height of the top compartment is adjustable, so tall cups like tumblers or wine glasses fit in quite easily. There is also a separate basket for cutlery, making sorting convenient, and the stress of having dishes piled up truly disappears. Honestly, the cleaning power was much better than I expected. I always thought that greasy dishes had to be washed by hand first, but after running it on the powerful wash cycle, they came out looking brand new—so clean that I wondered if I had really never touched them. The glass cups, in particular, came out sparkling clean without any water stains; it is a level of clarity that you can never achieve when washing by hand, so I felt it was worth the money just for that. And the drying power is what I was most impressed with. Perhaps thanks to TrueSteam, there is almost no water left when taking the dishes out. Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Thanks to the automatic door opening feature, any remaining moisture escapes naturally, preventing any musty smell. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. The noise level is also quieter than expected. I was worried because my kitchen and living room are connected, but I can barely hear the sound of it running when the TV is on. You just need to periodically take out the internal filter and rinse it with water, and since it has a stainless steel interior, dirt doesn't accumulate easily. The automatic detergent dispensing feature is so convenient that it automatically adjusts the amount once you fill it up initially; it was a revelation. It is truly convenient because I never forget to add detergent. Overall, the biggest change I noticed while using it is that **dishwashing has disappeared from the housework**. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Thanks to the automatic door opening feature, any remaining moisture escapes naturally, preventing any musty smell. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. You just need to periodically take out the internal filter and rinse it with water, and since it has a stainless steel interior, dirt doesn't accumulate easily. The automatic detergent dispensing feature is so convenient that it automatically adjusts the amount once you fill it up initially; it was a revelation. It is truly convenient because I never forget to add detergent. Overall, the biggest change I noticed while using it is that **dishwashing has disappeared from the housework**. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

The handles aren't overly flashy and are sleek, so it looks perfectly clean once installed as a built-in unit. At first, I didn't quite grasp how big a 14-place setting was, but once I actually use it, I realize every time just how big of an advantage that spaciousness is. There is still space left even after fitting 45 rice bowls, soup bowls, 2 pots, a frying pan, a cutting board, and several cups all at once. The bottom basket is designed for pots or large plates, and the height of the top compartment is adjustable, so tall cups like tumblers or wine glasses fit in quite easily. There is also a separate basket for cutlery, making sorting convenient, and the stress of having dishes piled up truly disappears. Honestly, the cleaning power was much better than I expected. To test the dishwasher, I intentionally put in stains from kimchi stew bowls and grease from pans, and I was quite surprised by how clean they came out. I always thought that greasy dishes had to be washed by hand first, but after running it on the powerful wash cycle, they came out looking brand new—so clean that I wondered if I had really never touched them. The glass cups, in particular, came out sparkling clean without any water stains; it is a level of clarity that you can never achieve when washing by hand, so I felt it was worth the money just for that. And the drying power is what I was most impressed with. Perhaps thanks to TrueSteam, there is almost no water left when taking the dishes out. Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Thanks to the automatic door opening feature, any remaining moisture escapes naturally, preventing any musty smell. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. The noise level is also quieter than expected. I was worried because my kitchen and living room are connected, but I can barely hear the sound of it running when the TV is on. You just need to periodically take out the internal filter and rinse it with water, and since it has a stainless steel interior, dirt doesn't accumulate easily. The automatic detergent dispensing feature is so convenient that it automatically adjusts the amount once you fill it up initially; it was a revelation. It is truly convenient because I never forget to add detergent. Overall, the biggest change I noticed while using it is that **dishwashing has disappeared from the housework**. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

Comments (English): [ LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-Place Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || To be honest, for a long time, I didn't trust dishwashers. I stubbornly stuck to washing dishes by hand, thinking it was just faster. However, during my recent kitchen remodel, everyone around me recommended them so strongly that I had no choice but to(?) get the LG Dios Objet 14-place setting built-in dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I honestly can't go back to washing dishes. The stress associated with "dishwashing" has completely vanished from my life. First off, when I saw the exterior after installation, the very first thought that came to mind was how beautiful it was. Thanks to the Objet’s signature subtle and luxurious matte finish, my kitchen suddenly looks like a hotel kitchen. I used to avoid buying dishwashers because I disliked how they stood out too much, but this one feels more like an interior design element than just an appliance. The handles aren't overly flashy and are sleek, so it looks perfectly clean once installed as a built-in unit. At first, I didn't quite grasp how big a 14-place setting was, but once I actually use it, I realize every time just how big of an advantage that spaciousness is. There is still space left even after fitting 45 rice bowls, soup bowls, 2 pots, a frying pan, a cutting board, and several cups all at once. The bottom basket is designed for pots or large plates, and the height of the top compartment is adjustable, so tall cups like tumblers or wine glasses fit in quite easily. There is also a separate basket for cutlery, making sorting convenient, and the stress of having dishes piled up truly disappears. Honestly, the cleaning power was much better than I expected. To test the dishwasher, I intentionally put in stains from kimchi stew bowls and grease from pans, and I was quite surprised by how clean they came out. I always thought that greasy dishes had to be washed by hand first, but after running it on the powerful wash cycle, they came out looking brand new—so clean that I wondered if I had really never touched them. The glass cups, in particular, came out sparkling clean without any water stains; it is a level of clarity that you can never achieve when washing by hand, so I felt it was worth the money just for that. And the drying power is what I was most impressed with. Perhaps thanks to TrueSteam, there is almost no water left when taking the dishes out. Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Thanks to the automatic door opening feature, any remaining moisture escapes naturally, preventing any musty smell. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. The noise level is also quieter than expected. I was worried because my kitchen and living room are connected, but I can barely hear the sound of it running when the TV is on. It was convenient because it is quiet enough to run at night without being a bother. Maintenance is also not difficult. You just need to periodically take out the internal filter and rinse it with water, and since it has a stainless steel interior, dirt doesn't accumulate easily. The automatic detergent dispensing feature is so convenient that it automatically adjusts the amount once you fill it up initially; it was a revelation. It is truly convenient because I never forget to add detergent. Overall, the biggest change I noticed while using it is that **dishwashing has disappeared from the housework**. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

Comments (English): [ LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-Place Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || To be honest, for a long time, I didn't trust dishwashers. First off, when I saw the exterior after installation, the very first thought that came to mind was how beautiful it was. I used to avoid buying dishwashers because I disliked how they stood out too much, but this one feels more like an interior design element than just an appliance. The handles aren't overly flashy and are sleek, so it looks perfectly clean once installed as a built-in unit. At first, I didn't quite grasp how big a 14-place setting was, but once I actually use it, I realize every time just how big of an advantage that spaciousness is. There is still space left even after fitting 45 rice bowls, soup bowls, 2 pots, a frying pan, a cutting board, and several cups all at once. The bottom basket is designed for pots or large plates, and the height of the top compartment is adjustable, so tall cups like tumblers or wine glasses fit in quite easily. There is also a separate basket for cutlery, making sorting convenient, and the stress of having dishes piled up truly disappears. Honestly, the cleaning power was much better than I expected. To test the dishwasher, I intentionally put in stains from kimchi stew bowls and grease from pans, and I was quite surprised by how clean they came out. I always thought that greasy dishes had to be washed by hand first, but after running it on the powerful wash cycle, they came out looking brand new—so clean that I wondered if I had really never touched them. The glass cups, in particular, came out sparkling clean without any water stains; it is a level of clarity that you can never achieve when washing by hand, so I felt it was worth the money just for that. And the drying power is what I was most impressed with. Perhaps thanks to TrueSteam, there is almost no water left when taking the dishes out. Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Thanks to the automatic door opening feature, any remaining moisture escapes naturally, preventing any musty smell. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. The noise level is also quieter than expected. I was worried because my kitchen and living room are connected, but I can barely hear the sound of it running when the TV is on. It was convenient because it is quiet enough to run at night without being a bother. Maintenance is also not difficult. You just need to periodically take out the internal filter and rinse it with water, and since it has a stainless steel interior, dirt doesn't accumulate easily. The automatic detergent dispensing feature is so convenient that it automatically adjusts the amount once you fill it up initially; it was a revelation. It is truly convenient because I never forget to add detergent. Overall, the biggest change I noticed while using it is that **dishwashing has disappeared from the housework**. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

To start with the conclusion, I honestly can't go back to washing dishes. The stress associated with "dishwashing" has completely vanished from my life. First off, when I saw the exterior after installation, the very first thought that came to mind was how beautiful it was. I used to avoid buying dishwashers because I disliked how they stood out too much, but this one feels more like an interior design element than just an appliance. The handles aren't overly flashy and are sleek, so it looks perfectly clean once installed as a built-in unit. At first, I didn't quite grasp how big a 14-place setting was, but once I actually use it, I realize every time just how big of an advantage that spaciousness is. There is still space left even after fitting 45 rice bowls, soup bowls, 2 pots, a frying pan, a cutting board, and several cups all at once. The bottom basket is designed for pots or large plates, and the height of the top compartment is adjustable, so tall cups like tumblers or wine glasses fit in quite easily. There is also a separate basket for cutlery, making sorting convenient, and the stress of having dishes piled up truly disappears. Honestly, the cleaning power was much better than I expected. To test the dishwasher, I intentionally put in stains from kimchi stew bowls and grease from pans, and I was quite surprised by how clean they came out. I always thought that greasy dishes had to be washed by hand first, but after running it on the powerful wash cycle, they came out looking brand new—so clean that I wondered if I had really never touched them. The glass cups, in particular, came out sparkling clean without any water stains; it is a level of clarity that you can never achieve when washing by hand, so I felt it was worth the money just for that. And the drying power is what I was most impressed with. Perhaps thanks to TrueSteam, there is almost no water left when taking the dishes out. Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Thanks to the automatic door opening feature, any remaining moisture escapes naturally, preventing any musty smell. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. The noise level is also quieter than expected. I was worried because my kitchen and living room are connected, but I can barely hear the sound of it running when the TV is on. You just need to periodically take out the internal filter and rinse it with water, and since it has a stainless steel interior, dirt doesn't accumulate easily. The automatic detergent dispensing feature is so convenient that it automatically adjusts the amount once you fill it up initially; it was a revelation. It is truly convenient because I never forget to add detergent. Overall, the biggest change I noticed while using it is that **dishwashing has disappeared from the housework**. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

Comments (English): [ LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-Place Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || To be honest, for a long time, I didn't trust dishwashers. I stubbornly stuck to washing dishes by hand, thinking it was just faster. However, during my recent kitchen remodel, everyone around me recommended them so strongly that I had no choice but to(?) get the LG Dios Objet 14-place setting built-in dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I honestly can't go back to washing dishes. The stress associated with "dishwashing" has completely vanished from my life. First off, when I saw the exterior after installation, the very first thought that came to mind was how beautiful it was. Thanks to the Objet’s signature subtle and luxurious matte finish, my kitchen suddenly looks like a hotel kitchen. I used to avoid buying dishwashers because I disliked how they stood out too much, but this one feels more like an interior design element than just an appliance. The handles aren't overly flashy and are sleek, so it looks perfectly clean once installed as a built-in unit. At first, I didn't quite grasp how big a 14-place setting was, but once I actually use it, I realize every time just how big of an advantage that spaciousness is. There is still space left even after fitting 45 rice bowls, soup bowls, 2 pots, a frying pan, a cutting board, and several cups all at once. The bottom basket is designed for pots or large plates, and the height of the top compartment is adjustable, so tall cups like tumblers or wine glasses fit in quite easily. There is also a separate basket for cutlery, making sorting convenient, and the stress of having dishes piled up truly disappears. Honestly, the cleaning power was much better than I expected. To test the dishwasher, I intentionally put in stains from kimchi stew bowls and grease from pans, and I was quite surprised by how clean they came out. I always thought that greasy dishes had to be washed by hand first, but after running it on the powerful wash cycle, they came out looking brand new—so clean that I wondered if I had really never touched them. The glass cups, in particular, came out sparkling clean without any water stains; it is a level of clarity that you can never achieve when washing by hand, so I felt it was worth the money just for that. And the drying power is what I was most impressed with. Perhaps thanks to TrueSteam, there is almost no water left when taking the dishes out. Plastic containers don't usually dry well, but compared to other products, this one dries much better. Thanks to the automatic door opening feature, any remaining moisture escapes naturally, preventing any musty smell. Items that are difficult to dry, such as lidded lunch boxes or tumbler lids, dry much better if you tilt them slightly before placing them in; once you get the hang of it, it is nearly perfect. The noise level is also quieter than expected. I was worried because my kitchen and living room are connected, but I can barely hear the sound of it running when the TV is on. It was convenient because it is quiet enough to run at night without being a bother. Maintenance is also not difficult. You just need to periodically take out the internal filter and rinse it with water, and since it has a stainless steel interior, dirt doesn't accumulate easily. The automatic detergent dispensing feature is so convenient that it automatically adjusts the amount once you fill it up initially; it was a revelation. It is truly convenient because I never forget to add detergent. Overall, the biggest change I noticed while using it is that **dishwashing has disappeared from the housework**. There were many times when I felt exhausted just thinking about the dishes left to wash after cooking, but now I just throw everything into the machine and press a button, and that's it—my quality of life has improved dramatically. Although the price was a bit steep at first, since it comes with a 10% cashback, my actual expenses were reduced, which made me feel less upset. Considering it is an appliance I use every day, I believe it was a well-deserved purchase. If you hate washing dishes, have wrist pain, or want to take care of your kitchen decor, you really won't regret buying this model. Even someone like me, who initially insisted I didn't need it, accepted it as a life partner in just one day. Personally, it is the most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year.

Sentence (English): I previously had a 12-person model.
Comments (English): [ I was surprised that it was bigger than the cooling. ] || ---------------- || I previously had a 12-person model. When my kids were little, they fell on the door, causing it to sag slightly. I had to get it repaired. However, frequent door opening errors and a broken temperature sensor led me to research and replace it. There were so many different models, all seemingly similar, that I decided to go with the more convenient option. Compared to my previous model, this one is noticeably more spacious, even though it's only for 2 people. It's great because it can hold a lot of pots and pans. However, there's a downside. There used to be a separate compartment for salt, but I don't know if it's because the specs have been upgraded, but it's inconvenient to have to put it in separately. I think it's okay to leave it out, but it's still inconvenient. And then there's the basket. The bottom of the inner basket is so wide that it's difficult to place small dishes there. Finally, I don't know if this is the case with all modern models, but the dishwashing time is incredibly long. If the dishwasher is set to 3 hours, the dishwasher will finish with about an hour left, and for the remaining hour, the door will automatically open and provide hot air and/or drying. It seems to be working, but I haven't used it for long, so I don't know if I set the dishwashing settings wrong or what, but I wonder if it really needs to be like this. The existing product doesn't have an automatic door opening, so other than those parts, it's still good because it's new.

Comments (English): [ LG appliances are subject to separate installation fees! ] || ---------------- || This is a review of a product I purchased with my own money. I visited an offline LG branch, but they were all full of insurance-like sales pitches, so I started searching online. As expected, the lowest price was Coupang, but it was almost 300,000 won less than the price quoted in-store, so I bought it right away. I purchased it a month before my moving date, and they scheduled the installation 2-3 days in advance, and it was done well on the appointed date. Unfortunately, my house had a dish drawer, and the removal of the drawer cost an additional 150,000 won. Even without the removal or installation fees, the LG branch was still cheaper, so I was satisfied. As a first-time dishwasher user, the cleaning power was excellent, but I definitely felt the need to sprinkle a little baking soda on greasy dishes or pre-clean them. It didn't clean things like dried rice, which I guess is just an inevitable limitation of the dishwasher. Also, because it's a touchscreen, the buttons sometimes felt a bit slow to respond, which was a minor inconvenience. Still, I like the design, and true to LG's motto, I'm satisfied with the daily wash cycle. I'm especially satisfied that I don't have to worry about drying it because of the hot air drying^^

I bought this because I like to cook and use dishes, but I hate washing dishes. It can hold a lot of dishes, large pots, and more without any problems. My purchase requirement was that it wouldn't affect the interior. Impressions from use. The intuitive controls make it easy to use. It's labeled in Korean with features like "quick" and "heat" cleaning, so you only need to know Korean to use it. It has a large capacity, as I wanted. I was a little worried before it arrived, but fortunately, it fits all my large pots. It feels like I've got an aunt. It's so convenient. I can just put it away after cooking and do other things, and it's still running. The only noise is the slightest noise. You can't help but hear the water draining and the sound of the water running. Oh, feel free to look up the trouble shooting guide on whirlpools website. yup all issues are "user error" and not their poor quality product.

Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher super quite ] || ---------------- || First everything that is great about this dishwasher. It washes dishes way better than out previous two units. It is super quite even though this wasn't a major concern for me it is nice. It dry's well with Crystal dry which is more effective and efficient (less energy than standard heated drying). Very little moistier left and only usually on plastic but not much.It holds a lot and is very flexible. I recommend watching the video on loading but once used to it we find it fits a lot more than our last model. The top tray is a big part of this. Yes, the silverware basket is smaller but part of that is keeping room for pans and dishes. Anything that doesn't fit in the basket or when its full goes in the top tray! The light and timer were worth the upgrade to me, the light isn't really inside, but it aims down at the rack, I didn't realize how nice this would be! Also, the timer is great to know how much time is estimated on the cycle, in auto mode the time can very based on how much soil is detected. When I did my test cycle the dishwasher was still out and it is cool to watch! This unit is tall, now it is measured at the same height and depth as standard units, but it is from front to back. We had elevated hardwood, so I had a hard time getting it in and had to lift our countertop to slide it in and then lower the countertop, everyone might not be able to get away with this.I hope it holds up well because it works great!

Sentence (English): We've been using this dishwasher for a few months now.
Comments (English): [ Smaller capacity than most, but very very quiet ] || ---------------- || We've been using this dishwasher for a few months now. It replaced a 10 yr old LG. While the LG had a lot more room, this one is by far superior. With that being said, it does have some issues. It cleans better than the LG, but the silverware rack could do a much better job (but is acceptable), and we have issues with how tall things can be loaded into the bottom rack. The middle rack can be raised and lowered, and we've even tilted it, but it still can't handle having a chef's or carving knife in the lower basket without the spinner hitting it. All large knives go into the middle rack now. The middle rack can be raised to accomodate some larger items on the bottom, but then you are compromised on the space between the middle rack and the silverware tray. On a good day, you won't have room to put most of your typical plastic lids and plastic containers on that middle rack anyway, and raising that rack makes it really tight. Everything bumps into the silverware rack, at that point. The sliverware rack 'wings' can also be adjusted, but that's only over the sides, and so the whole combination of adjustment options really just becomes a puzzle that can't be solved. Plastic, knives, bowls, tall glasses, all end up going wherever you can fit them. I assume that, since we can barely hear it running, that the extra space that would normally be in the interior, is now taken up by insulating the case, so it's quieter. If capacity isn't a concern for you, then this is a great dishwasher. It cleans moderately well, and the lack of sound can't be beat. Most of the time we have to check that it's still running, it's that quiet. If you want a meticulously spotless load, combined with capacity, keep looking. With all this said, I would buy this machine again. For the price point, and what we were looking for, it fits the bill.

It cleans better than the LG, but the silverware rack could do a much better job (but is acceptable), and we have issues with how tall things can be loaded into the bottom rack. The middle rack can be raised and lowered, and we've even tilted it, but it still can't handle having a chef's or carving knife in the lower basket without the spinner hitting it. All large knives go into the middle rack now. The middle rack can be raised to accomodate some larger items on the bottom, but then you are compromised on the space between the middle rack and the silverware tray. On a good day, you won't have room to put most of your typical plastic lids and plastic containers on that middle rack anyway, and raising that rack makes it really tight. Everything bumps into the silverware rack, at that point. The sliverware rack 'wings' can also be adjusted, but that's only over the sides, and so the whole combination of adjustment options really just becomes a puzzle that can't be solved. Plastic, knives, bowls, tall glasses, all end up going wherever you can fit them. I assume that, since we can barely hear it running, that the extra space that would normally be in the interior, is now taken up by insulating the case, so it's quieter. If capacity isn't a concern for you, then this is a great dishwasher. It cleans moderately well, and the lack of sound can't be beat. Most of the time we have to check that it's still running, it's that quiet.If you want a meticulously spotless load, combined with capacity, keep looking. With all this said, I would buy this machine again. For the price point, and what we were looking for, it fits the bill.

Sentence (English): How did I ever live without a dishwasher?
Comments (English): [ Accept the flaws and buy it ] || ---------------- || How did I ever live without a dishwasher? One-month review. Pros. * Cleanliness and squeakiness that's on a whole other level than hand washing. * The reliable 100°C True Steam sterilization function. * Not only is it beautifully designed, but it also dries dishes, eliminating the need for a dish drying rack in the kitchen. It's a great interior design feature. * It's complex and difficult to wash, so just throw in the sink drain strainer and other parts, the humidifier tank, cutlery holder, tumbler, side dish container (removable lid seal required), water purifier drip tray, etc., and you're done. (This is my biggest advantage.) * Controllable with the LG ThinQ app and downloadable programs for various dishes (top speed, full sterilization, plastic bowl mode, etc.). Cons. * You end up collecting dishes to run at once when using the dishwasher. -- I had to buy more because I ran out of dishes. * The dedicated detergent is more expensive than the Pong Pong, and maintenance costs like salt rinse are a concern. -- It's acceptable at 200-300 at a time. Water hardness varies depending on the region, so salt may be needed. I've noticed that adding rinse aid significantly speeds up the drying time, so I always use it. * There are certain dishes that can be washed in the dishwasher. -- Plastic and wooden utensils seem to be disappearing from my house. * It's a hassle to organize dishes. -- It's convenient to organize dishes right after eating and pre-washing. * Electricity bills will increase slightly. -- It varies depending on the progressive rate bracket, but it seems to cost a few thousand won more. * The cost of installing a dishwasher can increase depending on the kitchen layout. -- I've set aside money for a dishwasher, so the installation fee is about 50,000 won. * It takes an hour and a half to wash dishes? -- Two hours if you include drying. Two and a half hours if you add a rinse. But it's nice to be able to use that time without doing anything else. Sentence (English): I previously used a Samsung 12-person powerful dryer, but I bought this one when I moved.
Comments (English): [ It's the best ] || ---------------- || I previously used a Samsung 12-person powerful dryer, but I bought this one when I moved. It's great that it's a 14-person dryer with AI functionality that automatically washes clothes. Best of all, it's quieter during washing and draining than my previous 12-person model. It's practically silent. The door opens and closes smoothly. The way I organized things inside was different from my previous model, so I had a bit of a hard time playing Tetris. ^^;. It seems that the quieter it is, the longer it takes to wash clothes. Also, while it used to dry clothes well without the powerful drying feature, this one seems to dry clothes less quickly without it, so I always use the powerful drying feature. The installer said that while the AI feature is quieter, it reduces the cleaning power and takes longer. I bought it with the performance in mind, but this one is a bit disappointing. Had I known this would happen, I would have bought the hot air dryer.

Sentence (English): My first dishwasher: a Samsung 8-seater standing dishwasher (ODM from China), used for four years.
Comments (English): [ First dishwasher: Samsung 8-person standing (Chinese ODM), used for 4 years. Second dishwasher: Paco 12-person option when moving into apartment, used for 1.5 years. I recently got my third dishwasher. Samsung 8-person dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || My first dishwasher: a Samsung 8-seater standing dishwasher (ODM from China), used for four years. My second dishwasher: a Paco 12-seater dishwasher, which I purchased when I moved into my apartment, and used for a year and a half. I recently got my third dishwasher. The Samsung 8-seater dishwasher was a Chinese ODM, but it performed well. So, I decided to buy the Korean Paco, which was popular as a window air conditioner at the time, thinking it might be just as good as the Chinese one. I held out for a year and a half before finally replacing it recently. Since I started using a Samsung dishwasher as a newlywed, I've been a Samsung Things customer, so I've also used Samsung appliances for all my new home appliances. However, I've lost trust in the Infinity line refrigerator due to poor finish and noise, so I've chosen LG this time. I'll briefly list the pros and cons of this dishwasher compared to my previous one. 1. Noise: Low, quiet, incomparable to the two previous models. 2. Baskets: 3 compartments, deep, good storage, smooth rails, versatile, with a knife holder, scissors holder, frying pan holder, etc. 3. Notification sound: Pretty (the loud, annoying notification sound is a bit stressful), notification sound volume can be adjusted. 4. Remote control is possible. 5. Less water stains (no salt), water hardness can be managed. 6. Good cleaning power. 7. Build quality: Good (when replacing it, I noticed that the old dishwasher only had a sponge finish on the top, but the LG has a metal finish, the top heat insulation is good, and the sink top doesn't get hot). Additional power consumption: Approximately 450Wh for the regular course (no hot air drying). Approximately 980Wh for 40 minutes of regular course + hot air drying. Approximately 860Wh for 40 minutes of auto course + hot air drying. Steam has not been used yet (forgotten because it wasn't a feature). It's a bit disappointing that I can't choose the color, but I regret changing it now and feel satisfied that I made the right choice. #LGDishwasher, #DUE6BGL1E, #KitchenEssentials

Sentence (English): I'll share my review of the Samsung Bespoke 6-seater dishwasher I'm currently using.
Comments (English): I'll share my review of the Samsung Bespoke 6-seater dishwasher I'm currently using. Initially, I was concerned that its small size might lack cleaning power, but the water sprays evenly from the top and bottom, thoroughly washing even plates and cups. It sterilizes directly with water at high temperatures, ensuring hygiene. The claim of eliminating 99.999% of harmful bacteria is also true, as there's virtually no odor or residue after washing, which is a testament to its credibility. It doesn't require any installation, so it sits on a table, saving valuable space. The stainless steel interior dries quickly and cleanly after washing. The only downside is that it doesn't come with basic detergent, so I had to buy it separately. Still, I'm very satisfied with how much time I spend washing dishes each day.

Comments (English): [ Absolute piece of garbage ] || ---------------- || Absolute piece of garbage. It stopped working after three runs. Now it beeps uncontrollably after you start it and shows a red faucet sign. We tried to troubleshoot on our own, but none of the steps worked, it basically doesn't drain water. Then Homedepot support team sent me a link with a repair request form to a CANADIAN Bosch website which was obviously useless. I called Bosch support and they offered to send a technician in two weeks from now. So they're basically saying go ahead and wash your dishes by hand for two weeks after you paid almost 2k (with installation, parts and haul away), not to mention a week I waited for delivery. I negotiated a one week wait period after being on hold for some time and waiting for a call from their technician now (they can't even provide you the time of technician arrival during the call). Another cool thing is that people that Homedepot provided for the initial installation decided to do a test run without checking the insides of the dishwasher and run it with pieces of styrofoam and complimentary pack of dishwasher tabs in a plastic bag sitting inside.Now to the dishwasher layout. This is on me, I should have paid more attention, but I never assumed someone would design such an atrocity. I lived in four different countries switching multiple apartments and houses, I also travelled my fair share around the world staying in various Airbnbs, and NEVER in my life have I seen such a poorly designed dishwasher layout. The bottom rack is a complete waste of space with metal dividers positioned perpendicular to one another. The one side that is positioned atypically can't hold two rows of plates because of how the metal dividers spaced. Plates just don't fit next to each other (even smaller sized plates), even though the layout suggests that they should. On the right side there's a big gap with no dividers that doesn't serve any purpose.The top rack has the weirdest spacing between the rows. There're two rows that can't fit normal sized glasses (not to mention mugs) between the metal sticks. It's also very short because there's a silverware tray on top of it. I can't fit any tall tumblers on the top rack (like 20oz Yeti) if I don't lower it. BUT if I lower it to accommodate taller glasses and tumblers, then my dinner plates don't fit on the bottom rack, there's not enough space for them height-wise. It's like playing a crazy tetris game where you can't win. I feel like whoever designed this dishwasher is either an insane maniac or have never tried to load a dishwasher in their life.Also, the door doesn't drop down all the way when you start opening it, you have to manually lower it with your hand, which is a small thing but I find it annoying.Needless to say, I absolutely hate this dishwasher, I would not recommend it to anyone and I will never buy another Bosch product in my lifetime.ORDER # WJ***8, Model: SHX78CM5N/28, 0508

Sentence (English): I have owned this dishwasher for more than three years.
Comments (English): [ Dual Filtration design is insufficient ] || ---------------- || I have owned this dishwasher for more than three years. This dishwasher was great while it worked. Quiet operation and sparkling clean dishes. It has the selling point "Skip soaking, scrubbing and pre-rinsing with Dual Power Filtration". The filtration design on this unit is deeply flawed. There is a coarse screen which does not catch much food, resulting in the missed food to pass through the unit. My dishes typically only had trace amounts of food on them. The second filter is a fine mesh and is adjacent to the motor. Cleaning this filter requires a disassembly of the motor housing. This filter, if clogged, can prevent the unit from draining water properly, or the motor to burnout and fail. I first had an issue after two years of ownership with the error code E1F9, the tub not draining properly. I found a trick to get the error to clear, along with rinsing the dishes before loading, alleviated the issue for another year. Now, the issue is so frequent that I am going to replace the dishwasher (with a Bosch). The warranty for the unit after the initial year, only covers the tub, racks, and spray arms of the dishwasher. I do not see a point in having an appliance technician come out to replace $400 in parts and tell me that this will just happen again because of the poor design. If you purchase this dishwasher, be sure to rinse before loading or you will have issues. My suggestion is to avoid it entirely because the design is that poor.

Pros: * A level of cleanliness and squeaky-clean finish completely different from hand washing. * Sterilization function using 100°C steam. * The design is pretty, and since it dries the dishes, the dish drying rack has disappeared from the kitchen—great for interior design. * Just put in hard-to-wash items like strainers, drain filters and parts, humidifiers, cutlery holders, tumblers, and food containers (lid seals must be removed) and run it—that's it. * Controllable via the LG ThinQ app with various courses (Top Quick, Drum Sterilization, Plastic Dishes, etc.). Cons: * I end up accumulating dishes to run them all at once. -- I run out of dishes and have to buy extra. * The dedicated detergent is more expensive than dish soap, and there are maintenance costs for things like salt rinse aid. -- Even so, it can handle about 200-300 washes per cycle; salt may be necessary depending on water hardness in the region, and I always use rinse aid because I can really feel the drying time speeding up significantly. * There are specific types of dishes that can be washed in the dishwasher. -- It seems plastic and wooden tableware will gradually disappear from our house. * Electricity bill increased slightly. -- It varies depending on the progressive rate bracket, but it comes out to a few thousand won more. * There is a cost for custom cabinets depending on the kitchen layout. -- Since we set aside space to install a dishwasher cabinet, the installation fee was about 50,000 won. * It feels like an hour and a half to wash dishes? -- It takes two hours if you include drying. Two and a half hours if you add a rinse cycle. But I like that I can use my own time without doing anything else during that time; the quick wash takes 45 minutes! Now that I've used it, I realize there are many downsides, but the advantages are so great that I find myself using it all the time. The design doesn't clash with the kitchen at all. Comments (English): I spent a week comparing and analyzing countertop models to avoid a built-in one, and this is the product I finally picked! It features a toned-down white design, intuitive buttons, and great performance (I tend to pre-wash clothes). I received the very latest model, as its performance has been upgraded to Grade 2. Since it was out of stock, I received it as soon as it was back in stock, and the installation technician was very kind. A 28cm frying pan and a wok fit inside.
