Sentence (English): Absolute piece of garbage.
Comments (English): Absolute piece of garbage. It stopped working after three runs. Now it beeps uncontrollably after you start it and shows a red faucet sign. We tried to troubleshoot on our own, but none of the steps worked, it basically doesn't drain water. We also had to use our vet/dry shop vacuum for that, which I assume not every household has. Homedepot refused to take it back since more than 48 hours have passed since the installation (we even offered to exchange it for a more expensive model and pay more). Then Homedepot support team sent me a link with a repair request form to a CANADIAN Bosch website which was obviously useless. I called Bosch support and they offered to send a technician in two weeks from now. So they're basically saying go ahead and wash your dishes by hand for two weeks after you paid almost 2k (with installation, parts and haul away), not to mention a week I waited for delivery. I negotiated a one week wait period after being on hold for some time and waiting for a call from their technician now (they can't even provide you the time of technician arrival during the call). Another cool thing is that people that Homedepot provided for the initial installation decided to do a test run without checking the insides of the dishwasher and run it with pieces of styrofoam and complimentary pack of dishwasher tabs in a plastic bag sitting inside. Now to the dishwasher layout. This is on me, I should have paid more attention, but I never assumed someone would design such an atrocity. I lived in four different countries switching multiple apartments and houses, I also travelled my fair share around the world staying in various Airbnbs, and NEVER in my life have I seen such a poorly designed dishwasher layout. The bottom rack is a complete waste of space with metal dividers positioned perpendicular to one another. The one side that is positioned atypically can't hold two rows of plates because of how the metal dividers spaced. Plates just don't fit next to each other (even smaller sized plates), even though the layout suggests that they should. On the right side there's a big gap with no dividers that doesn't serve any purpose. The top rack has the weirdest spacing between the rows. Sentence (English): I hadn't bought a dishwasher before because it took up too much space and didn't seem like a necessity.
Comments (English): [ I didn't buy a dishwasher because it took up too much space and I didn't think it was absolutely necessary. But these days, maybe because of my age, washing dishes feels so tiring, so I want to be free from the stress of washing dishes. ] || ---------------- || I hadn't bought a dishwasher before because it took up too much space and didn't seem like a necessity. But lately, perhaps because of my age, I've found washing dishes to be a chore, so I decided to buy one to relieve the stress. It's Kota White, not the stark white of the sink. It's a shade with a few drops of gray, but I thought that was the color I was looking for, and it turned out fine. The color itself is a soft gray, which is beautiful. The renovation team visited first, removed a 600mm wide cabinet from the sink, and prepared a spot to install the dishwasher. Fortunately, the 600mm size fit perfectly, so there was no additional cost. They cut the mop holder into a U-shape. The cabinet that was removed had an opening at the top, so they used a slightly dirty piece of board they had and a little smaller than the depth of the cabinet to make a cover. I'm very satisfied and grateful that they did this without any additional cost. The cabinet can now be used as storage. The next day, the installer came, connected the water supply and drain pipes, and installed it. He kindly gave me simple instructions on how to use it. The dishwasher is slightly lowered towards the mop holder, so it's not perfect, but it's the best I can do given the circumstances, so I'm satisfied. I hesitated to buy a dishwasher because the process of purchasing and installing it seemed too complicated, but I figured I wouldn't be able to do it if I didn't do it while moving, so I just installed it. I don't think I'll ever have to wash dishes with a red face or get tired again. I'm just going to let it run wild. The installer told me that even if I run it every day, my electricity bill will only be around 5,000 won a month. Believe it or not, but since I invested so much time, money, and effort into installing the dishwasher, I hope it will continue to help me save energy and time.

But lately, perhaps because of my age, I've found washing dishes to be a chore, so I decided to buy one to relieve the stress. It's Kota White, not the stark white of the sink. It's a shade with a few drops of gray, but I thought that was the color I was looking for, and it turned out fine. The color itself is a soft gray, which is beautiful. The renovation team visited first, removed a 600mm wide cabinet from the sink, and prepared a spot to install the dishwasher. Fortunately, the 600mm size fit perfectly, so there was no additional cost. They cut the mop holder into a U-shape. The cabinet that was removed had an opening at the top, so they used a slightly dirty piece of board they had and a little smaller than the depth of the cabinet to make a cover. I'm very satisfied and grateful that they did this without any additional cost. The cabinet can now be used as storage. The next day, the installer came, connected the water supply and drain pipes, and installed it. He kindly gave me simple instructions on how to use it. The dishwasher is slightly lowered towards the mop holder, so it's not perfect, but it's the best I can do given the circumstances, so I'm satisfied. I hesitated to buy a dishwasher because the process of purchasing and installing it seemed too complicated, but I figured I wouldn't be able to do it if I didn't do it while moving, so I just installed it. I don't think I'll ever have to wash dishes with a red face or get tired again. I'm just going to let it run wild. The installer told me that even if I run it every day, my electricity bill will only be around 5,000 won a month. Believe it or not, but since I invested so much time, money, and effort into installing the dishwasher, I hope it will continue to help me save energy and time.

The downside: It's a built-in dishwasher, so the sink needs to be installed correctly. If it's not, the cost can be significant. Fortunately, I only had to remove one drawer, so it was installed without much trouble. Another downside is that if you move, you'll have to pay for removal and installation. If the installation location isn't right, the installation fee will increase. Of course, other products have similar installation costs. Still, thanks to the LG dishwasher, peace has returned to our home since yesterday. I hope you prosper! #LGDishwasher. #DUE6BGL1E #KitchenEssentials

Still, thanks to the LG dishwasher, peace has returned to our home since yesterday. I hope you prosper! #LGDishwasher. #DUE6BGL1E #KitchenEssentials

If the installation location isn't right, the installation fee will increase. Of course, other products have similar installation costs. Still, thanks to the LG dishwasher, peace has returned to our home since yesterday. I hope you prosper! #LGDishwasher. #DUE6BGL1E #KitchenEssentials

The downside: It's a built-in dishwasher, so the sink needs to be installed correctly. If it's not, the cost can be significant. If the installation location isn't right, the installation fee will increase. Of course, other products have similar installation costs. Still, thanks to the LG dishwasher, peace has returned to our home since yesterday. I hope you prosper! #LGDishwasher. #DUE6BGL1E #KitchenEssentials

After washing, the dishwasher starts a hot air drying cycle, and the automatic door opens to quickly dry the dishes. It's also very convenient for putting them away immediately. Overall, I'm completely satisfied with this appliance, giving it a 200 out of 100 for its design, cleaning power, noise, and convenience. It'll be less stressful to have to deal with the kids' piled-up dishes when my husband gets home from work early, so I feel like I made a good purchase. The downside: It's a built-in dishwasher, so the sink needs to be installed correctly. If it's not, the cost can be significant. Fortunately, I only had to remove one drawer, so it was installed without much trouble. Another downside is that if you move, you'll have to pay for removal and installation. If the installation location isn't right, the installation fee will increase. Of course, other products have similar installation costs. Still, thanks to the LG dishwasher, peace has returned to our home since yesterday. I hope you prosper! #LGDishwasher. #DUE6BGL1E #KitchenEssentials

Still, thanks to the LG dishwasher, peace has returned to our home since yesterday. I hope you prosper! #LGDishwasher. #DUE6BGL1E #KitchenEssentials

Sentence (English): This replaced a 21-year-old Whirlpool dishwasher that served us well.
Comments (English): [ Big improvement for my kitchen ] || ---------------- || This replaced a 21-year-old Whirlpool dishwasher that served us well. I'm very pleased with it after 2 weeks. It cleans dishes and pots far better, perhaps because of improvements to dishwashers in general over the past 20 years. We chose this ADA model because of space limitations in our particular kitchen layout, so I can speak to the ADA features. Things I like so far: • Third top rack for cooking utensils! This has gained back all the space lost to the non-standard ADA size, and more. • Nicely angled second rack slots for mugs and cups - no more puddles of water in the bases of mugs. • Door-open dry. Combined with the extended dry setting, plastics come out completely dry except for those molded plastics that have big crevasses that catch pools of water. All without subjecting my things to a super-heated air dry. • Delay timer. This is a must-have for me. • It doesn't require an app to run. I'll never buy an appliance that requires an app if I can avoid it. • It seems quiet. Things I don't like so much: • The utensil rack is inconvenient, in my opinion. I really miss the door-mounted utensil rack from our old Whirlpool, but none of the new ones have it. We turned out keeping our old rack and use it in the bottom shelf because it takes less space than the provided rack. Tip: When disposing of your old dishwasher, keep all the interior accessories. You can always throw them out later once you've figured out your new unit. • Some people may miss having a heated air dry, although I do not. My dishes are dry in the morning. It does have a sani-cycle that uses hot water to sanitize, if you need it. • No compartment for pre-wash detergent. I guess everyone uses pods these days, but I prefer powder so I can put a little detergent in the pre-wash. I just toss it in the tub. • I miss not having a display on the front to tell me how much time is left, or even if the delay start has been set. To see the status, you have to to open the door, look at the top-mounted control panel, press start/resume, then close the door.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher really delivers.
Comments (English): [ Bosch dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher really delivers. I use it regularly and can say it's simply solid. It cleans thoroughly, regardless of whether I load it with lightly rinsed plates or dishes after a large meal. It runs quietly, so you can turn it on in the evening and no one will complain about the noise. The drying function is also a strong point. After the program ends, dishes are dry and ready to put away, and the automatic door swing does the trick. It has a well-designed interior. Everything can be organized sensibly, including larger pots and pans, and the separate cutlery drawer is a big plus. It's also energy-efficient and doesn't seem to waste water or electricity. Sentence (English): Our GE dishwasher was installed in September 2025, and moved into our new house on October 4, 2025.
Comments (English): [ GE Service Goes Only So Far ] || ---------------- || Our GE dishwasher was installed in September 2025, and moved into our new house on October 4, 2025. We completed four loads of washing dishes with no issues. While working on the fifth load sometime in mid-October, the dishwasher stopped working and all lights on the display panel began to flash. We tried disconnecting power to the dishwasher for anywhere from five to 30 minutes, then reconnecting power. Every time, the dishwasher would not work and the display panel lights flashed continuously. We contacted GE and they sent a repair person from Sears. The repair person could not get the dishwasher into a diagnostic mode. He ordered and new display panel, control board, and door latch. All three parts arrived within several days, and the repair person returned to exchange the parts. After replacing the parts, the dishwasher did not work, and the display panel lights flashed continuously. At this point, the repair person told me that he "had done all he could." He recommended that I contact the company from whom our builder purchased our six GE appliances. Apparently, GE does not stand behind their warranty and offer to replace a unit that their own repair person deems unreparable. Fortunately, the company that our builder used to sell us our GE appliances stood behind their sale and exchanged our faulty GE dishwasher with a new unit they had in stock. I think it is deplorable that the GE repair person did not tell me that he would recommend that GE replace our dishwasher. I also think it is commendable that Reece Kitchen and Bath in Abilene stepped up and replaced our dishwasher with a new unit. They should be compensated by GE, but my guess is that GE is too big of a company to care about any one homeowner. God help us if our GE refrigerator, microwave, gas stove, clothes washer, and clothes dryer break down.

Sentence (English): The Delivery: The delivery crew initially delivered the wrong unit.
Comments (English): [ Shaky Delivery and Shady Installation Experience ] || ---------------- || The Delivery: The delivery crew initially delivered the wrong unit. Fortunately, we caught them just before they were about to pull away. They retrieved the unit and came back 30 minutes later with the correct unit. The installation: Costco used a 3rd party to install the Bosch unit in our home. Surprise! Surprise! We were informed by the installer that German-built Bosch dishwashers are not set up for ready installation in the U.S. The power wire apparently requires a modification. He “offered” to make the modification for $160. The alternative he said was to hire our own electrician to do it. It was impractical to try to get a representative from Costco on the phone to substantiate his claim. So we gave him the green light. He wanted the check made out to a person's name. Unclear if it was his, or a third party. No business card. No company name. No invoice. He said he would email me an invoice and a receipt. He never did. Very janky situation. The dishwasher is working fine. But you are rolling the dice with Costco for the “free” installation. If you are planning to purchase a Bosch, ask Costco about the issue of the power cord and how much over and above the “free installation” you are going to have to pay.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher is the worst appliance I have ever owned and easily the poorest quality product Samsung has ever put its name on.
Comments (English): [ Terrible Quality All Around ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is the worst appliance I have ever owned and easily the poorest quality product Samsung has ever put its name on. The top rack is already rusting in multiple areas which is completely unacceptable for a machine that is supposed to handle water every single day. The side mounting panels that hold the front fascia are cracked and flimsy, like they were made from the cheapest plastic Samsung could source.The final failure came when the wiring harness for the soap dispenser went bad. Nearly every major component has either broken, rusted or fallen apart. For a two year old appliance to be in this condition is outrageous. Save yourself money, time and frustration and avoid this model completely.At the same time we also bought a range that is deemed fire hazard by Samsung and a Bespoke fridge that try's to burn it self out because the engineers couldn't replicate the sealing technology that has been around for 30 years.

Sentence (English): I truly enjoy this dishwasher, but notable is the third rack.
Comments (English): [ I do love this machine ] || ---------------- || I truly enjoy this dishwasher, but notable is the third rack. What an amazing idea from someone. This third rack increases the capacity by a bigly amount because it takes all the large knives and spatulas that normally sit where glasses can go. It is new and so hasn't had time to really get calcium buildup from the well water. I have filters and soft water, but calcium still builds up. I'll keep an eye on that. But for now it cleans everything, the finish clean is wonderful. It even cleans up dried on food. I'm working on my husband actually pre cleaning his dishes. The last thing that finished up great was a corelle bowl full of refried beans that he set on the counter for a while.Now the so-so thing about this washer is the noise. I think it is really loud, but I live in a 700 sf house so I don't have any walls to separate the kitchen from the living room. It's only 10 steps away. So that may be why I only start it at night. Which brings me to the worst thing about this dishwasher. It DOES NOT have a delay start control function. All the control buttons are ok. Since I like to use my dishwasher when I'm either sleeping or out of the house because it's loud I miss the delay button from my old dishwasher.It seems to operate on normal cycle for a really long time. I haven't timed it but it seems like hours. I can't tell if its finger print proof since I have 3 mastiffs, I can tell you its not slobber proof.

Sentence (English): We bought this dishwasher from Home Depot on November 13, 2022.
Comments (English): [ Buyer Beware of this Model! ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher from Home Depot on November 13, 2022. Within 3 weeks of owning it, we began to have problems. It would not drain properly and it would not go through the cleaning cycles. We had the Home Depot warranty. To their credit, they stood behind the product and sent a repairman out. He told us what the problem was and did his best to fix it. Over the 3 years of ownership, we continued to have problems and Home Depot continued to honor their warranty. Finally on Nov. 14, 2025, the dishwasher again refused to work again. We had a repairman come out and he informed us that the motor had burned out and it would be at least $750 to put in a new one. We are, needless to say, going to buy a new dishwasher and send this one to the junkyard. Do NOT buy this model of Kitchenaid dishwasher unless you really want to see your repairman multiple times a year. It is nothing but trouble and not durable on top of that. This was a relatively expensive dishwasher. Kitchenaid used to have a good reputation. I had an old Kitchenaid diswasher that this one replaced (and that was still working! ) that lasted for 20 years. This one didn't even make 3 years! The last repairman advised us to go back to a more basic model that doesn't have all the \"bells and whistles.\" I'm taking his advice! (I do want to give kudos to Home Depot 3 year warranty. They did stand behind the dishwasher. unfortunately I guess we should've gotten the 5 year version, since this machine was only days out of warranty when it finally died.)

But for now it cleans everything, the finish clean is wonderful. It even cleans up dried on food. I'm working on my husband actually pre cleaning his dishes. The last thing that finished up great was a corelle bowl full of refried beans that he set on the counter for a while. Now the so-so thing about this washer is the noise. Since I like to use my dishwasher when I'm either sleeping or out of the house because it's loud I miss the delay button from my old dishwasher. It seems to operate on normal cycle for a really long time. I haven't timed it but it seems like hours. I can't tell if its finger print proof since I have 3 mastiffs, I can tell you its not slobber proof.

Sentence (English): I love my Bosch.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher, hard to operate ] || ---------------- || I love my Bosch. It replaced a mediocre dishwasher and does a far better job cleaning things. Main pain points: - the racks have opinions. All the prongs are angled, which makes tall things or pots/pans/sheet pans hard to slot in without wasting a lot of space. - the interface on the dishwasher is nice and simple. but means that I have to use the app to get most of the functionality. If I want to set it to start at 8pm, I have to remember to go to my phone to do that. - Maintenance mode is great! But it took me 5 minutes to find it. Much of the app is like that, largely unintuitive. But the dishwasher really works well, and is so quiet we have to again check the app sometimes to see if it's running.

Sentence (English): Having this dishwasher now for 3 months, I have come to the realization that Samsung didn't really take into account what people load into their dishwasher, and how the racks are completely useless.
Comments (English): [ Impractical capacity, poor rack design ] || ---------------- || Having this dishwasher now for 3 months, I have come to the realization that Samsung didn't really take into account what people load into their dishwasher, and how the racks are completely useless. Bottom rack has 4 rows of tines with large gaps on the bottom mesh, perfect for pot handles to drop below and hit the washing arm. Big 40 ounce Stanley metal tumblers tip over as there is not enough bottom support due to the large gaps, and while the tines themselves are nice that they fold out of the way, they will collapse easily when loading. What the bottom rack really needs is another 2 rows of tines to hold more cups, bowls and other smaller objects that could run on the bottom rack. The middle rack is of particular annoyance, as the height settings are impractical. Set it on low and the spinning spray nozzles hit on objects below like plates, baking sheets and Stanley mugs. Set it on the high setting to make sure there is enough clearance for objects below and then anything taller than a pint glass hits on the top plastic rack. And with plastic containers like snapware, the lid latches are ALWAYS catching on the plastic top rack. And that top rack…. Worthless! I'm strongly considering removing it altogether. I will say it does clean well, and removing the filter to clean is a snap. But overall, the racks are awful and impractical for washing dishes once or twice a day like in my house. I was able to load more in my old 2 rack dishwasher. Do better on your rack design Samsung!

Big 40 ounce Stanley metal tumblers tip over as there is not enough bottom support due to the large gaps, and while the tines themselves are nice that they fold out of the way, they will collapse easily when loading. What the bottom rack really needs is another 2 rows of tines to hold more cups, bowls and other smaller objects that could run on the bottom rack. The middle rack is of particular annoyance, as the height settings are impractical. Set it on low and the spinning spray nozzles hit on objects below like plates, baking sheets and Stanley mugs. Set it on the high setting to make sure there is enough clearance for objects below and then anything taller than a pint glass hits on the top plastic rack. And with plastic containers like snapware, the lid latches are ALWAYS catching on the plastic top rack. And that top rack…. Worthless! I’m strongly considering removing it altogether. I will say it does clean well, and removing the filter to clean is a snap. But overall, the racks are awful and impractical for washing dishes once or twice a day like in my house. I was able to load more in my old 2 rack dishwasher. Do better on your rack design Samsung!

Sentence (English): Delivery.
Comments (English): [ satisfaction ] || ---------------- || Delivery. I've often ordered garden products from Coupang, but this is the first time I've ordered something that required installation. I ordered a dishwasher, and a technician came to check the location to see if it was suitable. Less than an hour later, the installer arrived and installed it right away. We had ample phone conversations the day before the move, and they were punctual. Both the installer and the technician who arrived beforehand were very friendly, and the packaging was very meticulous. I'm very satisfied with the delivery. Price. The price fluctuated daily, probably due to the daily discounts. However, I believe I purchased it at the lowest price. The credit card discount made it even cheaper, which only made my satisfaction even greater. After purchasing and using it, I'm very satisfied with the purchase. I purchased it in-store. Even with the discount, I don't think I could have gotten it at this price. Details. The installer provided a very detailed explanation of how to operate the unit after installation. These days, scanning a QR code provides detailed instructions and can be easily operated via smartphone, making it easier to use. However, the technician was still very helpful and offered a tip that using a smartphone allows for greater functionality. He also explained the adjustable height of the upper compartment, including the use of detergent and conditioner, and explained that the lower compartment can be used for pots or slightly taller items, while the upper compartment can be used for simpler items like cups and bowls. When I actually started using the dishwasher with my phone, I found that it had far more functions than the ones on the top. Being able to set the settings on my phone and then run the program on the machine is incredibly convenient. However, the part where you select the operating time and function is located on the top, making it invisible from the outside, is a bit disappointing. Comments (English): [ The dishwasher I wanted all along! ] || ---------------- || I specifically sought this dishwasher out after using similar GE dishwashers at an Airbnb & my MILs home. I have purchased two Whirlpool brand (Kitchen Aid & Maytag) dishwashers in the past year. The Kitchen Aid had a critical failure out of the box where the vents leaked water all over my floors when the cycle was finished and door opened, after 3 tech visits and a control panel replacement it could not be fixed. I exchanged the Kitchen Aid for a Maytag with one vent but it would still dribble water out of the one vent when opening the door. We remodeled our kitchen this year and I decided to finally get this GE, which is the one I wanted all along. I like that it has no branding on the front and therefore matches my other stainless steel appliances. The vent on this dishwasher is hidden and not on the door so no more water dripping/leaking water on my new floors. IMO it has better space/capacity than the previous dishwashers. I can actually fit a 12" frying pan on the side without having to angle it sideways and take up extra space and the sprayer arm has plenty of clearance. I like how the dishes fit in the racks. The silverware is always extra clean due to the jets that sit under the utensil caddy. The spaces alloted for silverware in the caddy actually fit my silverware too, another issue I had with the prior dishwashers. Furthermore my clean dishes are DRY when I go to empty the dishwasher. Even plastic items are able to be put away immediately instead of having to air dry them on the dish rack for a few hours, which was a problem with the former dishwashers. I absolutely love this dishwasher and I'm so glad I finally bought it. The best part is that it was at least $200 less than the Whirlpool branded dishwashers I previously purchased. If you're on the fence I highly recommend this dishwasher!

Comments (English): [ I highly recommend SMI4EC ] || ---------------- || #opiniamotivowanapromoją I've had good experiences with Bosch appliances for years, and this dishwasher only confirms that. The attention to detail is evident, significantly extending the appliance's lifespan—even small features like the hidden door seal, which prevents cart wheels from rubbing against it every time the racks are pushed in. The dishwasher rinses dishes thoroughly, even removing detergent residue, which is a huge plus for me—I'm sure I'm not drinking any chemicals left over from previous wash cycles. Also noteworthy are the programs designed for maintenance and keeping the appliance in good condition. The AquaStop system, which provides a sense of security every day, is a major plus. I also appreciate the quiet operation, well-thought-out interior layout, and energy-efficient cycles, which don't compromise cleaning performance. Overall, it feels like a solid, well-made appliance designed to last for years. I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): It's always a crap shoot when buying appliances because you don't really know what you are going to get even when seeing things in person until you actually try to use them.
Comments (English): [ Poor Rack Design, Useless third rack ] || ---------------- || It's always a crap shoot when buying appliances because you don't really know what you are going to get even when seeing things in person until you actually try to use them. I bought mid-range dishwasher because this is not my forever home. This unit is a little louder than I expected, however, as I watched tv 20 ft away, the hour cycle didn't really bother me. It seemed to clean well, but not sure about the drying feature yet. The interior of the machine was very wet after a cycle, but the few dishes I washed were dry. So time will tell. The main problem I have is with the racks. The bottle jets and third rack sold me on this item. However, you cannot use the third top rack at the same time as the bottle jets or (even just placing a bottle in the normal top rack) if you want to place normal dinner plates in the bottom. I don't know if this was missed in production or what, but it's awful and I'm sorely disappointed. While you can choose to raise or lower the normal top rack, there are only two choices and there needs to be one in between. It's hard to explain without visuals which I cannot attach. But basically there is a two inch drop and there needs to be a 1" height drop option in order to be able to use the third rack, put bottles on the normal top rack, and place normal dinner plates in the bottom. I also do not like the tines at all. Weirdly spaced making it difficult to put items in the rack. Do not buy.

Sentence (English): I've had this dishwasher for about 2 years now and I haven't any major complaints about how it works.
Comments (English): [ 2 years in - mostly good ] || ---------------- || I've had this dishwasher for about 2 years now and I haven't any major complaints about how it works. Like some others say, its a bit slow but generally dishes have come out expectedly clean; that is to say that some hard and dried on things sometimes still remain after a wash (its not magic). I do like the middle rack moving up and down; though there usually isn't enough space on the lower rack to really drop it down but when i can it helps having that extra space for tall cups on the upper rack. I do wish I would have gone with a model that had wine glass holders.The one real complaint I have, which I'm not sure if is a problem with all dishwashers, is the tips at several points of the racks have deteriorated away and exposed rusty metal. Well it probably rusted after breaking. I haven't looked into how to address this because I don't see it being a problem at this point, but I would fix it if there was an easy guided way to do so. I've learned a lot about dishwashers since I bought this: preheat the waterline before turning the dishwasher on (by running sink water till its hot) and add small amount of soap on top of the closed soap dispenser. Both tricks help with cleaning a lot with any dishwasher.
